title: Adaptive Console UI: cross-platform layout and visual reliability fixes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a resilient, adaptive front-end layer for the Redwood Console that preserves layout fidelity and interaction parity across Chrome, Firefox, Safari (including iOS Safari), and Windows high-contrast modes. Scope covers dashboards (charts and cards), rollouts list + detail modals, and cost views (tables and cost summary). This ticket captures design artifacts, prototype links, visual QA notes, and handoff instructions for engineering. Key focus areas: 1) column collapse patterns for cost tables and numeric alignment for multi-currency costs; 2) canvas vs SVG rendering fallbacks for charts at different DPRs; 3) modal stacking rules and focus trapping for nested rollouts actions; 4) keyboard and screen-reader affordances for table row controls and chart legends; 5) cross-browser gap-filling for flexbox/sticky positioning inconsistencies. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens, interactive responsive prototype, cross-browser QA checklist, and annotated CSS token guidance for devs.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop (>=1280px), tablet (720–1279px) and mobile (<720px) layouts are defined in Figma with explicit collapse rules for each breakpoint
Cost table shows decimal-aligned numeric columns, currency symbol pinned left, and an optional per-row breakdown expansion; behavior documented for column hide/show on small widths
Charts render legible axes and tooltip content at DPR 1–3; fallback to SVG draw for Safari where Canvas smoothing causes axis jitter
Modal stacking: only one primary focusable modal; secondary confirmation uses non-disruptive bottom sheet on mobile and stacked dialog on desktop; keyboard focus never escapes visible modal
Rollouts list preserves row density and supports keyboard-driven canary toggle + associated confirmation flow (aria-live announcements for state changes)
Cross-browser visual QA checklist items (Chrome, Firefox, Safari macOS, Safari iOS, Edge) are marked done in the prototype review document
Dev handoff includes CSS variable tokens, icon asset variants, and a small set of utility classes for sticky summary bar and virtualized table rows
